clue.text: Gossips at dance discuss what they do for a living

definitions.text: discuss what they do for a living

parts.note: to gossip is to talk, so gossips is talks
a hop is an informal dance

explanation.surface: People chatting at a dance about their jobs.
explanation.definitionFit: To talk shop is the idiom for chatting about one's work, usually to the boredom of others.

indicators.note: in a down clue, going uphill means the word is read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: in golf, to top the ball is to hit a poor drive across its upper half

explanation.surface: A stain left by someone driving clumsily up a slope.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uphill' turns TOPS round to give the answer; topping is a golfing fault, not a motoring one.
explanation.definitionFit: A spot is a small mark or blemish, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: They have a belief in British industry

indicators.note: the answer sits inside the words British industry, running across both

explanation.surface: Some people have faith in the strength of British manufacturing.
explanation.definitionFit: Followers of a religion are people who hold a belief, and Hindus are one such faith group.

definitions.meaning: baffled, unable to proceed or answer
dismissed in cricket when the wicketkeeper breaks the stumps with the batter out of the crease

explanation.walkthrough: Cricket: a batter who leaves the crease can be dismissed by the wicketkeeper knocking off the bails, a mode of dismissal with this name.
explanation.definitionFit: Being puzzled is being stuck, and in cricket a batter put out by the keeper is so dismissed.

clue.text: How mince is cooked by Chinese?

indicators.note: cooking something alters it, so the letters of how mince are reworked

parts.note: taken as written as the fodder

explanation.surface: Asking how minced meat is prepared in Chinese cooking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is cooked' rearranges HOW MINCE; 'by' is a link, and 'Chinese' is the noun for a Chinese meal.
explanation.definitionFit: A Chinese, as in a takeaway meal, is the class to which this noodle dish belongs as an example.

clue.text: Plant part is said to be regenerated

indicators.note: regenerating rebuilds something in new form, so these letters are reformed

parts.note: taken as written as the fodder

explanation.surface: A gardener claims a piece of a plant will grow back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be regenerated' rearranges PART IS SAID.
explanation.definitionFit: The aspidistra is a hardy houseplant, an example of a plant.

clue.text: Soldiers give up and fall back

parts.note: RE is the Royal Engineers, a British Army corps
to cede is to surrender or give up

explanation.definitionFit: To recede is to move back or withdraw, a synonym of falling back.

clue.text: Feature film put on before the big fight

definitions.text: Feature film put on before the big fight

parts.words: Feature film put on before the big fight
parts.note: not a cinema programme: a feature is a facial feature, and a film is a thin coat applied to the face before battle

explanation.definitionFit: Warriors traditionally daub colour on their faces before battle, a thin coating applied ahead of the fight.

parts.note: told someone to be quiet, saying the word for silence

explanation.definitionFit: Someone who silences others by saying 'sh!' is admonishing them to be quiet.

indicators.note: away means the letter for right is removed from the garment

parts.note: a skirt is a garment

explanation.surface: Instructions to remove a piece of clothing at once.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Take off' reads as a verb about undressing, but it is the noun: a take-off is a parody.
explanation.definitionFit: A take-off is a parody or imitation, and a skit is a short comic sketch doing just that.

parts.note: dumb means stupid
a waiter is an attendant at table

explanation.definitionFit: A dumbwaiter is a small lift carrying food between floors, a kind of lift.

indicators.note: on board means placed inside the ship, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: SS is a steamship, the board one is on
hock is German white wine

explanation.surface: Bottles of wine carried aboard ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jars' looks like a noun for containers, but it is the verb: jolts.
explanation.definitionFit: To jar is to jolt or startle, a synonym of the verb to shock.

clue.text: May I not revel playing a form of bridge?

parts.note: may I not is can't I, giving the letters in order

indicators.note: playing about with the word revel rearranges its letters

parts.note: taken as written as the fodder

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether they may not enjoy a game of bridge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'playing' rearranges REVEL into LEVER; 'May I not' gives CAN'T I, and the bridge is a structure, not the card game.
explanation.definitionFit: A cantilever bridge is built from projecting arms supported at one end, a form of bridge.

parts.note: to eye something is to watch it
a liner is a passenger ship

explanation.surface: Instructions to apply cosmetics while keeping an eye on a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: Eyeliner is a cosmetic, so it is a kind of make-up.

clue.text: Assembled ships, an armada, was so described

definitions.text: Assembled ships, an armada, was so described

indicators.note: assembling puts parts together in a new order, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A fleet gathered and given a name in history.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Assembled' rearranges SHIPS AN; the rest of the clue points to the armada of 1588.
explanation.definitionFit: The great fleet sent against England in 1588 was called the Armada of Spain.

clue.text: War that's breaking out in Panama?

indicators.note: breaking out suggests disorder, so the letters are scattered and rearranged

parts.note: taken as written as the fodder

explanation.surface: A conflict erupting in a Central American country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'breaking out' rearranges WAR THAT'S. 'Panama' looks like the country, but it is a type of hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A Panama is a lightweight woven hat made of plant fibre, a kind of straw hat.

parts.note: not an obsession: the letter B begins the word bonnet

explanation.definitionFit: The letter starting a word is its first letter, and bee, the letter B, starts bonnet.

clue.text: Hero achieves eminence amongst top men

indicators.note: amongst places one word inside the other

parts.note: aces are top performers
an eminence is a hill

explanation.surface: A champion rises to fame among the best.
explanation.definitionFit: Achilles is the greatest Greek warrior of the Iliad, a classical hero.

clue.text: Tack on finish to a literary supplement

parts.note: to tack on is to add
end means finish

explanation.surface: Adding an ending to a book's appendix.
explanation.definitionFit: Addenda are material added to a book, a supplement to the text.

parts.note: not a drinks bar on a plane: a metal rod holding carpet on a flight of steps

explanation.definitionFit: A rod holding carpet in place on each step is a bar fitted to a flight of steps.

parts.note: not bootleggers: people brewing tea need no licence, and they use this vessel

explanation.definitionFit: A pot for brewing tea is a vessel, and tea brewers need no licence.

definitions.meaning: like the fruit with downy skin

explanation.definitionFit: Peachy is slang for excellent and literally means resembling the fruit.

indicators.note: on means the piece for go follows the piece for mate

parts.note: a pal is a mate, a friend
a go is a try, an attempt

explanation.surface: An apology followed by encouragement to a friend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sorry' looks like an apology, but it is the adjective: a sorry sight is a poor one.
explanation.definitionFit: Sorry can mean pitiful or meagre, as in a sorry state, matching worthlessly small.

parts.note: not a gun at a race: a turning wheel driven by a mill race, the channel feeding a mill

explanation.definitionFit: A mill race is the channel of water that turns a mill's wheel, which revolves.
A thin coating is a film, and a flick is slang for a movie.

indicators.note: heartless means the middle letter of the word for devil is removed

parts.note: a fiend is a devil

explanation.definitionFit: To track down something is to locate it, a synonym of finding it.

clue.text: Possibly take work in state capital

indicators.note: in places one piece inside the other
possibly signals the letters of take may be arranged another way

parts.note: taken as written as the fodder
op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: Perhaps accepting a job in a US state capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possibly' makes TEKA, and 'in' puts the work inside it; the surface's job-taking hides that 'state capital' is the definition, a US state.
explanation.definitionFit: Topeka is the capital city of the US state of Kansas.

indicators.note: into places one word inside the other

parts.note: a deed is an action
rang means called, phoned

explanation.surface: A dog barks when summoned to act.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Barking' looks like a dog's noise, but it is British slang for mad, as in barking mad.
explanation.definitionFit: Barking, short for barking mad, means crazy, a synonym of mentally unbalanced.
